name: GeoCalib
plain: GeoCalib (ETH Zurich / Microsoft, 2024): the camera of one photo (focal length, field of view) and how it is tilted (roll, pitch from gravity), from perspective fields and an optimisation; no checkerboard needed. Apache-2.0 code, CC-BY-4.0 weights; training photos of mixed licences.
summary: GeoCalib (Veicht et al., ECCV 2024): single-image camera calibration. An MSCAN-L network predicts per-pixel perspective fields (up vectors and latitude) with confidences; a differentiable Levenberg-Marquardt optimiser fits the focal length and gravity direction (roll, pitch) to them. Gives intrinsics, gravity, roll, pitch and vertical field of view.

papers.title: GeoCalib: Learning Single-image Calibration with Geometric Optimization

limitations: The Levenberg-Marquardt loop branches and logs on its convergence (35 graph breaks: `torch.compile` runs with breaks, no `torch.export`); its damping, singularity check and early stop are batch-wide, as upstream, so a batch is one problem and an image's result can depend on its batch mates.

The standalone FP32 TensorRT benchmark accelerates the 416 x 320 field predictor and uses the usual PyTorch camera optimizer. On 97 portrait LaMAR images the largest angle difference was 0.000048 degrees.
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: the camera intrinsics `[3, 3]` and, where the model estimates them, the gravity direction in the camera frame, roll, pitch and vertical field of view.

variants.name: geocalib-pinhole

training_data.name: OpenPano (perspective crops of public 360-degree panoramas: PolyHaven, HDRMaps, AmbientCG, BlenderKit)

licence.training_note: Trained on OpenPano (README, paper Sec. 4): perspective crops of ~2.8k public 360-degree panoramas (PolyHaven, HDRMaps, AmbientCG, BlenderKit). Only the weights licence (CC-BY-4.0) counts for the commercial flag.

variants.input_size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32

original16.protocol: median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input, original code at the pinned commit, torch.no_grad; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls
original16.note: torch.autocast(float16) around the call; cvg/GeoCalibdedb29f94fc GeoCalib.calibrate (pinhole), its kornia resize / crop / LM fit

portable.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5
portable.note: The eager Levenberg–Marquardt fit reuses the image pixel grid, residuals and weights. All five camera output tensors match on one synthetic input and eight labeled LaMAR photos.

quality.title: LaMAR2k, all 2000 images, roll / pitch / vertical FoV error AUC@5 degrees %
quality.protocol: Each image at its own size (1440 x 1920 portrait); roll, pitch and vertical field of view of the fitted camera against the ground truth; AUC of the error up to 5 degrees (errors below 1 degree count as 1, siclib's `compute_auc(min_error=1)`), the GeoCalib paper's protocol.

portable32.note: The TensorRT field estimator uses separate plans for portrait and landscape images. Both modes run the same camera optimizer on the original input size.

tensorrt.note: The TensorRT field estimator uses separate plans for portrait and landscape images. Both modes run the same camera optimizer on the original input size.

Every 20th LaMAR image in its original orientation and size. The compiled mode accelerates field prediction and keeps the camera fit eager.

portable32.note: Matched subset rescored from saved portable FP32 outputs.

compile.note: Compiled field prediction followed by the eager camera fit, using both aspect ratios at native size.

quality.title: LaMAR2k, 97 portrait images from every 20th entry, angle AUC@5 degrees %
quality.protocol: Each image at its own size (1440 x 1920 portrait); roll, pitch and vertical field of view of the fitted camera against the ground truth; AUC of the error up to 5 degrees (errors below 1 degree count as 1, siclib's `compute_auc(min_error=1)`), the GeoCalib paper's protocol. Take every 20th LaMAR image and score the 97 portrait images at their original size. In TensorRT mode only the 416 x 320 field predictor is accelerated.

portable32.note: The TensorRT field predictor feeds the regular PyTorch camera optimizer.

tensorrt.note: The TensorRT field predictor feeds the regular PyTorch camera optimizer.

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.0032 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.087 and p99 <= 0.39 (absolute error of the output `intrinsics`).
